problem:
The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{1}{{e}^{t}+1}\cdot q(t).
$$

Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t=0,$ if 

$$
\begin{aligned}q(0)=⟨1,\sqrt{2},1⟩,\,{q}^{′}(0)=⟨1,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
worked_solution:
First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{{e}^{t}+1}\cdot q(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{{e}^{t}+1})\cdot q(t)+\frac{1}{{e}^{t}+1}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(q(t)) \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{t}}{({e}^{t}+1)^{2}}\cdot q(t)+\frac{1}{{e}^{t}+1}\cdot {q}^{′}(t) \\  \\ {T}^{′}(0) & =-\frac{{e}^{0}}{({e}^{0}+1)^{2}}\cdot q(0)+\frac{1}{{e}^{0}+1}\cdot {q}^{′}(0) \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}q(0)+\frac{1}{2}{q}^{′}(0) \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}⟨1,\sqrt{2},1⟩+\frac{1}{2}⟨1,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(-⟨1,\sqrt{2},1⟩+2⟨1,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},0⟩) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}⟨1,0,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(0)‖ & =\frac{1}{4}\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(0)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve at the point where $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(0) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(0)}{‖{T}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{4}⟨1,0,-1⟩}{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4})} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨1,0,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $T$ and $N$ at the point where $t=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0)\cdot N(0) & =\frac{1}{2}q(0)\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨1,0,-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨1,\sqrt{2},1⟩\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨1,0,-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}(1(1)+\sqrt{2}(0)+1(-1)) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}(1+0-1) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$
